name: vasculitis overview
title: Vasculitis: a new headache over 50 points to giant cell arteritis, sinus, lung, kidney and nerve disease to ANCA-associated vasculitis, purpura on the legs to cutaneous leukocytoclastic vasculitis, and an identifiable cause to secondary vasculitis; each column gives presentation, numbered investigations and treatment in order

root.title: Systemically unwell, several organs, purpura: is it vasculitis, and which?
lines: every patient: head-to-toe history and exam · blood count, creatinine, liver enzymes, sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP), urinalysis · chest X-ray
kidneys and lungs can be SILENT · rule out INFECTION before immunosuppressing

head: h
Giant cell arteritis (GCA)
large vessel · the most common vasculitis
only over 50 (most over 70)
inv: • or Doppler 'halo sign' in specialty centres
tx: after blood is drawn · NEVER wait for results

head: h
ANCA-associated vasculitis
anti-neutrophil cytoplasmic antibody · small vessel
granulomatosis with polyangiitis (GPA)
microscopic (MPA) · eosinophilic (EGPA)
inv: 2 · ANCA ONLY if small vessel suspected
• negative does NOT rule it out
tx: Unstable, lung bleed, renal failure → ADMIT

head: h
Cutaneous leukocytoclastic vasculitis
small vessel · alone or part of another type
inv: • purpura: punch biopsy in primary care
• ulcer: deep excision by a surgeon
tx: only if severe, other agents failed, infection excluded

head: h
Secondary vasculitis
an identifiable underlying cause
pres: • infection: hepatitis B or C, HIV, other

panels.title: Suspect primary vasculitis when
items: chronically unwell: fevers, chills, weight loss
multi-organ failure: lung hemorrhage + renal dysfunction
AND no infection or cancer found

panels.title: Classify by vessel size
items: small: ANCA trio, cryoglobulinemia, cutaneous leukocytoclastic, Henoch-Schönlein
